import math

# 50 US states IRS receipts unemployment insurance taxes 2020 (in thousands of dollars)
values = [64332, 10983, 109606, 122270, 735828, 97255, 64286, 27166, 417974, 222639, 
          17231, 34037, 271859, 100945, 49175, 66239, 61165, 62871, 18204, 101598, 
          161146, 178509, 170442, 31420, 119199, 15993, 35205, 45885, 20345, 187735, 
          19766, 350082, 190438, 12812, 235458, 60206, 71863, 257446, 25975, 65892, 
          12334, 169376, 536530, 60537, 8471, 162666, 209293, 13475, 117667, 7638]

# Sort in descending order
sorted_values = sorted(values, reverse=True)
print("Top 10 values (sorted descending):")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values[:10]):
    print(f"{i+1}: {v}")

# Hill estimator with k=7
k = 7

# Get the top k+1 values
X_k_plus_1 = sorted_values[k]  # The (k+1)th largest value (X_(k+1))
print(f"\nX_{k+1} = {X_k_plus_1}")

# Calculate sum of log(X_i / X_{k+1}) for i=1 to k
log_sum = 0
print(f"\nCalculating Hill estimator:")
for i in range(k):
    X_i = sorted_values[i]
    log_ratio = math.log(X_i / X_k_plus_1)
    log_sum += log_ratio
    print(f"i={i+1}: X_{i+1}={X_i}, log({X_i}/{X_k_plus_1}) = log({X_i/X_k_plus_1:.4f}) = {log_ratio:.6f}")

print(f"\nSum of logs: {log_sum:.6f}")

# Hill estimator: alpha = k / sum of logs
alpha = k / log_sum
print(f"\nHill estimator (Pareto tail exponent) = {k} / {log_sum:.6f} = {alpha:.6f}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {alpha:.3f}")
